pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a singing game, who gives the instructions? (1 mark)
   A. The audience only
   B. The oldest pupil always
   C. The soloist
   D. Nobody

2. Why should you not rush the last lines of a page? (1 mark)
   A. It is not allowed
   B. Neatness can be lost when you hurry
   C. The pen will break
   D. The page will run away

3. When copying a sentence, what should you check? (1 mark)
   A. Only the colour of the pen
   B. Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   C. Only the page number
   D. Only the date

4. A good comment during a gallery walk is (1 mark)
   A. This is ugly
   B. Nothing to say
   C. You cannot write
   D. Your spacing is very even

5. Which of these is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Close the door.
   B. A door has a handle.
   C. The door is red.
   D. The door was open.

6. What should a reader do at a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Skip a line
   B. Shout
   C. Turn the page
   D. Pause briefly

7. What should listeners do after a group reads aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Leave the room
   B. Give kind and helpful feedback
   C. Laugh at the readers
   D. Tear the script

8. Which word must begin with a capital letter in the middle of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Monday
   B. morning
   C. cloud
   D. weather

9. What should you do to check the punctuation in your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   B. Write it again without looking
   C. Tear it
   D. Cover it

10. What is wrong with: it rained all night. (1 mark)
   A. It needs a capital letter at the start
   B. It needs no changes
   C. It needs two full stops
   D. It needs a comma after it

11. What is a cue in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. The last words of the person before you
   C. A title
   D. A full stop

12. What is a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. A title
   B. One word
   C. A group of sentences about one main idea
   D. A page number

13. Which sentence has a verb? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau and his face.
   B. The red bag.
   C. In the morning.
   D. Kamau washed his face.

14. What is a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A group of animals
   C. The order in which things happen
   D. A type of word

15. What is the difference between a proverb and a story? (1 mark)
   A. They are the same
   B. A proverb has many characters
   C. A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   D. A story is shorter

16. What does a peer review checklist help with? (1 mark)
   A. Ending the lesson
   B. Stealing ideas
   C. Checking a partner's story kindly
   D. Cleaning the room

17. What does A stitch in time saves nine mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sewing is easy
   B. Stitches are costly
   C. Nine is a lucky number
   D. Fix small problems early

18. What should you do with the events of a story you tell? (1 mark)
   A. Tell them in the order they happened
   B. Never mention the end
   C. Mix them up
   D. Skip the beginning

19. Which word joins two ideas that contrast? (1 mark)
   A. because
   B. but
   C. and
   D. so

20. Which is an example of caring for an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving it without shelter
   B. Beating it
   C. Throwing stones at it
   D. Giving clean water every day

21. Which word means not inside? (1 mark)
   A. outside
   B. between
   C. beside
   D. under

22. Which is a good tip for reciting? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the floor and mumble
   B. Speak very fast
   C. Look at the audience and speak clearly
   D. Cover your face

23. Which adjective describes colour? (1 mark)
   A. large
   B. tall
   C. thin
   D. silver

24. Which is a polite phrase to ask someone to repeat? (1 mark)
   A. Say it again now
   B. Could you repeat that, please?
   C. Stop talking
   D. What did you say?

25. Which adjective describes size? (1 mark)
   A. tiny
   B. round
   C. red
   D. soft

26. What is an advertisement? (1 mark)
   A. A lesson
   B. A weather report
   C. A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   D. A poem

27. Which is a polite phrase for asking someone to explain again? (1 mark)
   A. Say it again now
   B. Pardon me, could you explain?
   C. Never mind
   D. You are silly

28. What are images in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Words that make pictures in the mind
   B. Maps
   C. Photographs
   D. Diagrams

29. What is repetition in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Changing the title
   B. Repeating words or lines for effect
   C. Adding a picture
   D. Deleting lines

30. In writing, what is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A story
   C. Words telling someone what to do
   D. A poem

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

32. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

33. Choose one proverb and explain its meaning. Then describe a real situation at school where it would apply. (5 marks)

34. Create a form with four fields to find out classmates' favourite games. Include a title and instructions. (4 marks)

35. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)

36. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

37. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

38. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

39. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)

40. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

41. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

42. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)

43. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)

44. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

45. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

46. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

47. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — The soloist
   The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

2. B — Neatness can be lost when you hurry
   Careful writing should stay the same to the end.

3. B — Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   These are the points of neat copying.

4. D — Your spacing is very even
   Kind and specific comments help writers.

5. A — Close the door.
   Close the door tells you what to do.

6. D — Pause briefly
   Full stops tell us to pause.

7. B — Give kind and helpful feedback
   Feedback helps readers improve.

8. A — Monday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

9. A — Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   Reading aloud helps find where pauses and stops belong.

10. A — It needs a capital letter at the start
   The first word of a sentence must begin with a capital letter.

11. B — The last words of the person before you
   You come in when you hear your cue.

12. C — A group of sentences about one main idea
   A paragraph has one main idea.

13. D — Kamau washed his face.
   Washed is the verb.

14. C — The order in which things happen
   Sequence means order.

15. C — A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   Proverbs are very short.

16. C — Checking a partner's story kindly
   Peer review helps improve writing.

17. D — Fix small problems early
   Early action prevents bigger trouble.

18. A — Tell them in the order they happened
   Order helps listeners follow.

19. B — but
   But shows contrast.

20. D — Giving clean water every day
   Water and shelter meet its needs.

21. A — outside
   Outside means not inside.

22. C — Look at the audience and speak clearly
   Eye contact and clarity help.

23. D — silver
   Silver is a colour.

24. B — Could you repeat that, please?
   Please and could show politeness.

25. A — tiny
   Tiny describes size.

26. C — A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   Adverts promote products or services.

27. B — Pardon me, could you explain?
   Pardon me and could you are polite.

28. A — Words that make pictures in the mind
   Images are word pictures.

29. B — Repeating words or lines for effect
   Repetition emphasises an idea.

30. C — Words telling someone what to do
   Instructions say what to do.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct proverb with a sensible meaning and a matching situation, for example A stitch in time saves nine means fix small problems early, such as mending a small tear in a uniform before it grows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the proverb, two marks for the meaning and two marks for a clear situation.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Title: Favourite Games. Instructions: Write neatly. Fields: Name, Class, Favourite game, Date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for title, one for instructions, two for four fields.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.
